sanitizedRequest.prompt:
Write as an experienced British healthcare copywriter.

Using only the verified information supplied for this selected area, return two clearly separated plain-text fields and nothing else.

HERO INTRODUCTION:
Write 35–55 words introducing Pharmacy First for people in the selected area and naming Vision Pharmacy as the provider.

LOCAL INTRODUCTION:
Write 170–230 words in three fluent British-English paragraphs.

Paragraph 1:
Introduce the area, its location and its character using verified facts.

Paragraph 2:
Describe meaningful verified landmarks, green spaces, shopping, community facilities and healthcare references. Select the most useful facts and connect them naturally. Do not list every evidence record.

Paragraph 3:
Move naturally from the area and its local healthcare needs into Vision Pharmacy’s Pharmacy First service. Name Vision Pharmacy and Pharmacy First, and explain that eligible patients can receive a pharmacist consultation for certain common conditions. Do not reproduce a fixed clinical closing sentence. The transition must feel like part of the article—not a disclaimer pasted onto the end.

You may express only this Pharmacy First meaning:
- Vision Pharmacy provides Pharmacy First consultations for eligible people from the selected area.
- Pharmacy First covers certain common health conditions.
- The pharmacist assesses symptoms, relevant medicines and medical history.
- The outcome may include advice, suitable treatment or referral to another healthcare professional.
- Eligibility and treatment depend on the individual clinical assessment.

Do not claim guaranteed treatment, guaranteed medicine supply, walk-in availability, faster care, convenience, immediate or prompt treatment, that a GP appointment is never required, travel time, route distance or easy access, or any unverified pharmacy service or outcome.

Do not write travel time, route distance, kilometres, or that the pharmacy is easy to reach. Do not locate the pharmacy in the premises locality in these fields; that belongs later on the page. Do not invent facts or reuse wording or facts from another area.

Use neutral factual British English. Do not describe an area as pleasant, welcoming, vibrant, thriving, attractive, popular, desirable, close-knit, well-connected, convenient or ‘known for’ something unless that exact character claim is supported by the supplied evidence. Describe verified places, facilities and organisations naturally without inventing an opinion about the area.

Do not use: “orient yourself”; “orientating pharmacy care”; “local orientation”; “familiar points around”; “listed as”; “recorded as”; “named on the provider page”; “recorded healthcare setting”; raw provider labels; or evidence-source language.

Do not repeatedly use the area name. Use natural alternatives such as “the area”, “the neighbourhood”, “local residents” and “the community” where appropriate.

Return exactly this layout:
HERO INTRODUCTION:
<one paragraph>

LOCAL INTRODUCTION:
<paragraph 1>

<paragraph 2>

<paragraph 3>
Selected area: Blaby
Confirmed pharmacy name: Vision Pharmacy
Confirmed pharmacy premises locality: Oadby
Saved straight-line distance: approximately 6.7 km in a straight line
Verified landmarks, parks, shopping, civic and community facilities:
- Blaby Library (with Family Hub support) is a community facility in Blaby.
- Blaby & District Social Centre is a community facility in Blaby.
- Blaby & Glen Parva Community Service is a community facility in Blaby.
Verified GP practices or healthcare facilities:
- NHS general practice services in Blaby are provided from Northfield Medical Centre in Blaby.
Approved Pharmacy First service meaning:
- Vision Pharmacy provides Pharmacy First consultations for eligible people from the selected area.
- Pharmacy First covers certain common health conditions.
- The pharmacist assesses symptoms, relevant medicines and medical history.
- The outcome may include advice, suitable treatment or referral to another healthcare professional.
- Eligibility and treatment depend on the individual clinical assessment.

rawResponse:
HERO INTRODUCTION:
Vision Pharmacy provides the NHS Pharmacy First service for eligible residents in Blaby. Through this service, patients experiencing certain common health conditions can receive a clinical consultation with a pharmacist, who assesses their symptoms to deliver appropriate health advice, suitable treatment or referral to another healthcare professional.

LOCAL INTRODUCTION:
Blaby is an established settlement in Leicestershire defined by its civic amenities and local public services. The area serves as a focal point for local residents, offering access to essential community infrastructure and healthcare provision that supports people across the neighbourhood.

Key facilities in the area include Blaby Library, which offers community access to books and information alongside integrated Family Hub support. Public activities and local social support are hosted at the Blaby & District Social Centre, as well as through the Blaby & Glen Parva Community Service. Medical care for local residents is centred around Northfield Medical Centre, which delivers primary NHS general practice services to the community.

To support local healthcare access, Vision Pharmacy provides Pharmacy First consultations for eligible people from the area. This service covers certain common health conditions, allowing patients to speak with a qualified pharmacist who carefully assesses their symptoms, relevant medicines and medical history. The outcome of each consultation depends entirely on individual clinical assessment, with options ranging from professional advice and suitable treatment to referral to another healthcare professional.
